title: Project — Shop Billing and Stock Manager

blocks.html: After completing this project you will be able to:

items.html: go through the full software development cycle: problem, plan, algorithm, code, test and improve
design data with parallel arrays and divide work into functions
validate input and handle mistakes made by the user
test a program systematically with a test table
present and defend your project in a viva

blocks.html: Vidya Stationery is a small shop near a school in Patna. The owner writes every bill by hand and often finds out that an item has run out only when a customer asks for it. She wants a simple computer program that can:

items.html: show the list of items with code, price and stock;
make a bill for a customer, refusing items that are out of stock;
give a 5% discount when the bill is Rs 1000 or more;
add new stock when goods arrive;
show a daily report of items sold, total sales and items running low (fewer than 5 left).

blocks.html: This chapter builds that program step by step using everything you learned in Chapters 15 and 16.

blocks.html: The shop sells 6 items. Each item has a code, a name, a price, the quantity in stock and the quantity sold today. We use five parallel arrays — the same index refers to the same item in every array.
Two global variables keep today's totals: todaySales (money collected) and billCount (number of bills).

blocks.html: Did you know? Billing software in real shops works on the same ideas — item codes, stock records and validated input. The barcode on a product is simply its item code printed as lines, so that a scanner can type the code for the cashier.

Software is developed in steps: requirement analysis, design, algorithm, coding, testing and documentation.
Parallel arrays store related data; a search function such as findItem() turns a code into an index.
Dividing the program into functions keeps main() short and each job easy to test.
Input validation rejects wrong codes, wrong quantities and requests above stock.

items.html: Why did you use functions? To keep each job separate, keep main() short, and test each part on its own.
Why parallel arrays and not separate variables? Six items would need 30 variables; arrays let one loop handle all items.
What happens if the user types a code that does not exist? findItem() returns −1 and the program prints “No item with code …”.
How do you stop a bill from selling more than the stock? The quantity is compared with stock[i] before the sale is accepted.
Why are todaySales and billCount global? Both makeBill() and dailyReport() need them, and they must keep their values between bills.
What is the limit on lines in one bill? 20, the size of lineItem and lineQty .
What is lost when the program closes? All sales and stock changes, because nothing is saved to a file.
How did you test the discount rule? With subtotals of 999, exactly 1000 and 1850.
Canteen billing: Adapt the project for the school canteen with at least 10 food items, a daily report of the most popular item and a low-stock alert.

Bus ticket counter: Store 5 routes with fares and seats. Book tickets, refuse when seats are full, and print a report of tickets and money collected per route.
